objectives: Match the letters m, s, t and a to their taught sounds.
Blend printed graphemes to decode simple CVC words.
Read familiar CVC words without relying only on pictures.
concepts: Decoding connects printed graphemes to known phonemes.
A CVC word can be decoded from left to right.
The learner should sound out, blend and then check the whole word.

definitions.definition: Using known letter-sound relationships to read a printed word.
A letter or group of letters representing a speech sound.

commonMistakes: Guessing from a picture instead of reading the letters.
Reading letters in the wrong order.

basic: Decode mat, sat, map and tap.
Match printed CVC words to spoken words.
conceptual: Explain how decoding differs from guessing.
Identify the grapheme representing each sound.
application: Read a printed word and select its meaning.
Decode a word without picture support.
higherOrderThinking: Identify why a learner's decoded word is incorrect.
Choose the best correction when a learner skips a grapheme.
mixedReview: Mix grapheme recognition, decoding, sound sequence and word meaning.

mistakeBasedRevision: If a learner guesses from a picture, cover the picture and decode the letters.
If a sound is skipped, point to each grapheme in sequence.
weakTopicRevision: Read ten familiar CVC words and repeat any word that was decoded incorrectly.

activities.name: Sound buttons
steps: Sweep under the word while blending.

activities.name: Read and match
steps: Learner matches it to the spoken word or picture.

activities.name: Picture-free reading
steps: Show familiar CVC words without pictures.

outcomes: Learner decodes at least 8 of 10 familiar CVC words correctly.
Learner reads familiar CVC words without depending on picture guessing.
